title: Shiny UI Infrastructure for JSON-Driven React Rendering
text: minimal app.R. UI lives www/ (ui.js, plus ui.css want styles — discovered automatically); server owns reactive computation: reactive_output() sends JSON-serializable value unchanged; client reads useShinyOutputValue("greeting"). Push data client send_message(). Traditional Shiny renderers (e.g. plotly::renderPlotly()) work , rendered client-side ShinyOutput React component — binding JS/CSS discovered render function delivered client automatically, *Output() placeholder needed. See examples/01-hello/ complete runnable app (app.R alongside equivalent app.py, sharing one www/ client). Run without cloning:
code: library(shiny) library(shinyreact)  ui <- page_react() # discovers www/ui.js + www/ui.css  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$greeting <- reactive_output({     paste0("Hello, ", input$name, "!")   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server) shiny::runGitHub("posit-dev/shinyreact", subdir = "examples/01-hello")

title: Shiny UI Infrastructure for JSON-Driven React Rendering
text: wire_tap() (test-; requires shinytest2 package) records JSON payloads cross Shiny websocket, can assert values server actually delivered values client actually sent: expect_* matchers value (identical()) function (truthy), retrying timeout; all_output_values() / all_messages() / all_input_values() return channel’s full history. Python counterpart shinyreact.playwright.WireTap.
code: test_that("dist_data bins the waiting column", {   app <- shinytest2::AppDriver$new(     app_dir,     options = list(shiny.trace = TRUE)   )   withr::defer(app$stop())    tap <- shinyreact::wire_tap(app)   tap$expect_input_value("bins", 30L)   tap$expect_output_value("dist_data", function(d) d$breaks[[1]] == 43) })

title: Tap the websocket wire of a shinytest2 app — wire_tap
text: Cross-channel frame order (output lands first, outputs batch single values frame, busy/progress interleaving) reactive-scheduling coincidence, contract — tap deliberately expose global frame stream. Within one channel (one output id, one message type, one input id) wire order guaranteed, expect_* methods consume cursor: expectation scans recorded history just past previous match, values arrive checks never missed — capture lossless; polling decides re-scan. Successive expectations one channel therefore assert ordered subsequence. Python counterpart shinyreact.playwright.WireTap, methods semantics. One small divergence: jsonlite::fromJSON() maps JSON null output value NULL, indistinguishable absent key, early output: null frames dropped Python sees None.
